title: Add opt-in `--allow-remote` helper that adds a program-scoped firewall rule
description:
Implement the owner-approved explicit Windows firewall helper, preserving the complete original hud-lgb6c.2 outcome: `tze_hud.exe --allow-remote` performs one opt-in elevated operation that adds or updates one program/TCP/port/tailnet-scoped Windows Firewall allow rule and removes inbound BLOCK rules for this exact program; `--disallow-remote` restores the helper's prior firewall state, including those removed BLOCK rules. A non-elevated invoking owner gets one UAC prompt and sees the child's actual result. An already elevated owner uses the same operation without another prompt. Nothing installs, starts the HUD, changes listeners, or elevates implicitly.

Authority is the full original hud-lgb6c.2 fields and parent hud-lgb6c owner decision dated2026-10-06, docs/scope.md T6(2)-(3), current docs/vision.md trust/cheap-idle principles, docs/api.md identity/operator boundary and invariants. Keep loopback plus Tailscale binding, per-user install/autostart without admin, paired PSK/allow authentication and five MCP tools. The old loopback-only proposal was superseded by the actual parent decision and is not an option. This is an implementation bead, not a detection/docs-only replacement.

Current source is1b5eff5fd9e8e02161d78ecb222a93c51256ccc0. Detection PR1341 actually MERGED2026-10-06T00:46:34Z, squash766123ea0e1fd497d7439c4cc6c6ffaf0f979a32 is reachable from this pin. Its actual firewall.rs uses INetFwPolicy2, per-port allow union, program environment expansion, a5s lazy cache, /admin/status and pairing warnings. Its Rule is intentionally a diagnostic subset; the reader skips some failed attributes and enumeration failures can end the loop. That reader cannot authorize deletion or serve as a restoration backup. No new detection engine is requested.

The exact program is the executable the owner intentionally invoked: installed `InstallPaths.exe` when this invocation is that canonical install, otherwise the current explicitly launched in-place/dev executable. Never silently choose a different installed HUD merely because its file exists. Canonicalize this real file before elevation, freeze its identity and the invoking owner's context, and require the elevated child to be the same executable. There is no public arbitrary program argument. Effective listen ports are current StartupOptions: explicit CLI overrides the invoking process's TZE_HUD_MCP_PORT/TZE_HUD_GRPC_PORT, then9090/50051 defaults;0 disables that listener. RawRuntime TOML has only profile and safe_mode_hotkey, not port members. Do not invent config keys or read legacy [network]. Accept the existing --config context, validate an explicitly supplied file with the existing resolver/validator, and tell the owner to use the same CLI/env port overrides as the running HUD. Do not discover settings by probing the owner host or starting a listener.

The original least-privilege allow rule remains named `tze_hud (tailnet)`, enabled inbound ALLOW TCP, this canonical ApplicationName, sorted unique nonzero LocalPorts, RemoteAddresses100.64.0.0/10,fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, all profiles and no edge traversal. Same-program inbound BLOCK cleanup remains mandatory, including different protocols/ports/profiles and disabled rules; removing only the new allow rule is not full undo. Save complete selected rules before any mutation and restore their actual properties on undo. The journal's sole authority is that original reversibility and safe retry; no broad policy export/import or unrelated rule management.

Non-goals: changing bind/interface filtering, adding LAN/wildcard/UDP permissions, third-party firewall engines or GPO, implicit install/startup/pairing/admin-endpoint elevation, deployment, owner Windows verification, cache clock changes, pairing styling, new auth/API/config keys, broad policy framework, source guards or test farms. hud-bstmy.1.18 owns the5s cache clock; hud-h51u7.8.3 owns pairing styling. Owner-only live UAC/firewall/pairing/publish/undo verification remains the existing hud-lgb6c.3 outcome; reconciliation remains hud-lgb6c.4. No new owner wait or prerequisite is invented.

This packet was produced once in FIRST source/metadata shaping with Tests:+0 ~0 -0. It contains no implementation or gate execution. ROOT must apply these full fields and separately ACK an execution bootstrap; Cargo and caches require a later explicit exclusive lease. The worker never writes Beads lifecycle. Preserve the prior5.7 author worktree and its accepted evidence.
design:
1. Current owners and control flow. app/tze_hud_app/src/main.rs owns StartupOptions190/default242, parse_options363, early actions877-895, InstallPaths/Action dispatch894-918 and WindowedConfig ports1116-1117. Add a narrow RemoteAction::{Allow,Disallow} option and documented public flags to that parser; dispatch the one-shot helper immediately after parsing and before attach-info/pair/install/cleanup_old_exe/single-instance/config boot/agents/GPU/network. Reject a remote action mixed with install/uninstall/purge/pair/attach-info/handoff/update/benchmark/quiescent actions, both remote modes, repeated mode flags, malformed private payload or unexpected positional inputs. Ordinary startup and per-user install::Request/Action semantics remain unchanged. The private child payload is parsed before normal environment-backed StartupOptions so an alternate administrator's environment cannot retarget the ports or start a runtime. Public flag parsing stays in the existing parser; the private payload is a strict internal interface, not another public configuration surface.

2. Narrow module boundary. Keep the existing firewall.rs diagnostic code and FirewallProbe default/caller behavior. Add firewall/remote.rs, exposed as firewall::remote for the app's actual caller. Put a pure typed RuleSpec, exact-program BLOCK filter, transaction decisions and test adapters there; put all token/Shell/COM/filesystem-security operations in its cfg(target_os="windows") backend. Off Windows, the explicit public helper returns a documented nonzero Windows-only result without touching the filesystem, elevating, starting the HUD or pretending success. Reuse existing windows0.58/serde/serde_json/getrandom dependencies. Use existing workspace sha2 through a narrow runtime dependency only if needed for the persistent canonical-program key; no new third-party dependency. Add only demonstrated Windows feature gates: Win32_UI_Shell, Win32_System_Environment, Win32_Security_Authorization and Win32_Globalization if CompareStringOrdinal is used; current Registry/Security/Threading/FileSystem/Com/Ole/Variant/WindowsFirewall features already cover the other calls. No app Windows dependency is needed because FFI stays in runtime.

3. Invoking owner and target. Resolve current_exe and the canonical file via an actual file handle/GetFinalPathNameByHandleW, remove only the extended path prefix for comparison, and use ordinal Windows case-insensitive identity; do not use basename, substring, an uncanonical relative path or a different installed exe. InstallPaths::same_path is a navigation/existing launch helper, not a substitute for file identity. An installed invocation has paths.exe identity; any explicit in-place/dev invocation remains current_exe even if another install exists. Freeze the two already parsed ports, disabled0 state, initiating PID/creation time and original token identity before UAC. Explicit --config is validated using the current schema but never supplies nonexistent TOML port fields; no agent store or secrets are read. The child validates its actual current executable against the frozen target and the initiating process image/creation time; resolves the original owner's token rather than its elevated administrator's APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA. Use that token for ExpandEnvironmentStringsForUserW of rule ApplicationName; request TOKEN_QUERY|TOKEN_DUPLICATE|TOKEN_IMPERSONATE as the primary API requires. Unknown/unexpandable/uncanonicalizable candidate identities are not interpreted as this program. If a candidate cannot be adjudicated and backed up safely, abort preflight before mutation and print the limitation. Never substitute the administrator's profile or guess an identity. Already elevated public invocations use their own context. No public target-path flag is added.

4. Explicit UAC and child lifecycle. Only a valid public Allow/Disallow action can call the launcher. GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation) must establish actual elevation; the private child flag alone grants nothing. A non-elevated private child exits nonzero without invoking runas again. For a normal non-elevated owner, ShellExecuteExW uses lpVerb runas, absolute lpFile of this same executable, UTF16 argument buffers and SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS|SEE_MASK_NOASYNC. Initialize an appropriate COM apartment for Shell on its private launcher thread and pair cleanup; do not interfere with winit/tokio apartments. Construct only allowlisted private fields: version/mode, same-program identity, validated ports, original parent PID/creation time and a128-bit result nonce. Quote each Windows argument by the documented backslash/double-quote rules; no shell, cmd.exe, PowerShell, environment expansion of the command line or string concatenation of arbitrary startup flags. Reject embedded NUL/ill-formed or oversized payloads before Shell. ERROR_CANCELLED is cancellation, not success, and changes no firewall/journal state. Missing hProcess, launch failure, failed wait or invalid child exit/result is nonzero; never infer child success from Shell success. Wait for actual child termination and call GetExitCodeProcess, close handles on every branch. Choose synchronous owner-controlled waiting until the one-shot child actually exits, not a timer that kills a mutating process mid-transaction; no second UAC prompt or retry loop. UAC time remains controlled by the owner. A crash/interrupted parent is handled through the durable transaction journal, not an assertion that Windows COM writes are atomic.

5. Result transport. Shell elevation is not a reliable stdout-capture protocol. The child writes one bounded, non-secret per-nonce result beneath the protected helper-owned machine directory, containing the operation, canonical program/ports, each actual changed rule name, final policy classification, exit status and rollback/recovery state. The parent reads only its deterministic nonce path after its actual child terminates, validates version/nonce/program/operation and prints those changes/result, then deletes that result using DELETE permission granted only on that specific result file to the original owner SID. The directory and journal remain admin/SYSTEM writable; grant read access required for this result, never generic user directory/file write permission. Do not accept an arbitrary output/request path from the unprivileged parent. Unique nonce files prevent a second command from replacing the first parent's result. Missing/corrupt result cannot turn an unsuccessful child into success. Orphaned result cleanup is bounded to helper-owned names during a later explicit operation, never background startup/frame work.

6. Rule specification and ownership. RuleSpec is pure and complete: Name=tze_hud (tailnet), program canonical identity, Protocol6, Direction inbound, Action allow, Enabled true, Profiles NET_FW_PROFILE2_ALL, LocalPorts sorted/deduplicated nonzero decimal ports, RemoteAddresses both exact tailnet CIDRs, unconstrained LocalAddresses/RemotePorts/Interfaces only where required for normal TCP, edge traversal disabled and no extra service/app-container/user/IPsec restrictions. If both listeners are0, Allow refuses before elevation rather than issuing wildcard ports; Disallow still finds/restores an existing journal irrespective of current ports. Tag the helper allow with a stable Grouping/Description/version/program-key marker and verify both marker and full current fingerprint. An unowned rule with the fixed name, a different-program helper rule, duplicate ambiguous fixed-name entries, a missing journal for an existing tagged rule, or edited ownership attributes is a preflight collision; do not overwrite, adopt or delete it. Print the collision and exact scoped remedy. Repeated same-program Allow updates only its own rule and keeps the first baseline; it never creates duplicate allows or broadens to another exe. Installed and dev exe paths do not silently replace one another under the shared approved name.

7. Exact BLOCK filter and complete restoration image. Select INetFwRule Direction inbound and Action BLOCK only when ApplicationName resolves to this same canonical program under the original owner context. Do not select absent/empty/any-program applications, another program, outbound rules or generic port-only blocks. Keep the original selection independent of enabled/profile/protocol/port state; disabled or currently inactive same-program blocks can matter later and belong in the undo image. Read all relevant properties with errors propagated, including Name, Description, ApplicationName, ServiceName, Protocol, applicable LocalPorts/RemotePorts or ICMP types/codes, LocalAddresses/RemoteAddresses, Direction, typed Interfaces, InterfaceTypes, Enabled, Grouping, Profiles, EdgeTraversal, Action and available INetFwRule2/3 edge/user/package/machine/security properties. Do not serialize arbitrary VARIANT memory; support the actual typed interface-string array and reject unsupported shapes. Getter/enumerator/cast failures or properties that cannot safely be recreated stop before any mutation. INetFwRules::Add explicitly does not support a nonempty LocalAppPackageId, so such a selected rule must fail closed, not be deleted and reconstructed approximately. Preserve complete exposed rule behavior/properties; opaque Windows-generated rule identifiers may change on recreation and are not claimed to be preserved. Do not reuse the diagnostic to_rule Option or treat an enumeration error as end-of-list.

8. Name-safe deletion/restoration. INetFwRules::Remove accepts a name, while Add can overwrite an existing identifier; never call Remove on an unqualified shared display name. For selected BLOCK objects use unique helper-owned temporary aliases recorded in the journal before renaming, verify the exact aliased object's full fingerprint and uniqueness, then Remove only that alias. This allows same-display-name rules to be isolated without deleting foreign name peers. Restore through unique recorded aliases and then restore each original Name, checking the complete original property multiset after each operation. Add properties in protocol-correct order on a fresh NetFwRule COM object before adding it; preserve enabled/profile/security state rather than relying on COM defaults. If the platform cannot reproduce a selected rule's complete supported properties/name multiplicity safely, fail preflight before deletion. Do not claim this platform contract proved by pure mocks: native non-policy COM object checks and the existing owner verification explicitly exercise its limits. All alias operations are scoped to already selected exact-program rules, compensatable and recorded; no persistent alias is accepted as a successful final state.

9. Journal and serialization. Before the first COM write, create a versioned per-canonical-program journal below SHGetKnownFolderPath(FOLDERID_ProgramData)/tze_hud/firewall, not an environment-selected or alternate administrator's per-user path. Its sole contents are the prior helper allow state, complete selected BLOCK restoration images, exact current/intended owned fingerprints and each prepared/applied/undo phase. It is not a global policy backup. Verify existing root/directory/file owner+DACL, reject reparse points/foreign or writable-by-unprivileged paths, and create helper-owned nodes with protected admin/SYSTEM write permissions; preserve all unrelated ACLs and installation directories. Obtain an exclusive share-zero lock-file handle for this program transaction across processes/sessions, before read/preflight/write. Busy returns nonzero without waiting/relaunch loops. Atomically replace and flush the protected journal before each mutation intent and record its verified completion; never overwrite the first baseline on a retry. New later same-program BLOCK rules are appended durably before their own removal. Missing/unsupported/corrupt journal, unexpected owned state or identity mismatch fails closed. Disallow does not need the original config or current ports, only the same program identity and validated journal.

10. Forward/undo/recovery. Allow preflights admin permission/local policy modify state, full rule snapshot, ownership/name safety, restorable properties, journal durability and original owner identity. Add/update the owned least-privilege allow, then isolate/remove all selected same-program BLOCK rules, preserving each restoration image. Verify actual rule properties and re-read policy using the existing decide function with the selected program/ports. Successful exit0 requires the applied operation and, for Allow, an actual Allowed classification under that detector; Unknown/Blocked cannot be printed as allowed. If another generic block/GPO/third-party policy still blocks, print the limitation and compensate this attempt to its prior owned state rather than touch that unrelated rule. Any failed write, remove, verification or durability step attempts reverse-order compensation; restore BLOCKs before removing/reverting the allow, and retain the recovery journal on incomplete compensation. Disallow restores all journaled original BLOCK properties/names and the original allow baseline, verifies the original semantic policy multiset, then removes the completed journal/owned lock artifact when safe. No-journal/no-owned-rule Disallow is a successful no-op, not a claim that the firewall is globally blocked. A repeated Allow or interrupted Disallow first reconciles prepared/applied entries against exact observed owned fingerprints; idempotent retry never duplicates a restored rule or loses a saved BLOCK. An external administrator's concurrent edit is a conflict: our lock coordinates our own commands only; reread fingerprints before each change, do not overwrite that edit in compensation, preserve the journal and identify the unresolved scoped operation. COM lacks multi-rule transactions; never claim stronger atomicity.

11. Trust and reporting limits. The added rule grants only program/TCP/current-port/tailnet remote access and leaves listeners on loopback+tailnet. Removing an existing all-address same-program BLOCK can also uncover permissions from preexisting broader ALLOW rules; it is therefore false to claim that this cleanup proves the entire machine policy can never permit LAN-source traffic. Do not create/modify those broader allows or a new policy engine; print removed rules' actual scopes, keep them in the undo image, document this approved cleanup interaction, and leave unrelated/third-party engines unchanged. The existing detector is policy-derived and has current diagnostic limits, not a real remote probe. Its5s cache in an already running HUD may remain stale until its normal expiry; no cross-process invalidation/API/cache-clock repair is requested. Update FIX_HINT to the actual --allow-remote command with a brief same-port-override instruction and use it in the existing blocked pairing line. Preserve state/reason/rule/error JSON names, lazy evaluation, blocked-only warning and other card lines. Same-target/ports plus a fresh cache are prerequisites for the documented Allowed observation; owner .3 separately proves real pairing/MCP from the tailnet.

12. Fixtures and gate species. Extend main.rs::tests::parse_options_accepts and parse_options_rejects using their existing Env/ENV_VAR_MUTEX factory: modes, mutual exclusions, unchanged normal defaults,0 listeners, CLI>env ports and invalid private/public argument combinations. Extend pairing::tests::firewall_warning_line_only_when_blocked with the delivered command hint while preserving3 quiet/4 blocked lines. Add exactly five justified new feature behavior tests in firewall::remote, as no existing detection fixture executes firewall mutation/undo/elevation: (a) rule_spec_uses_resolved_program_and_ports, a table of installed/in-place canonical target, default/override/zero/dedup ports and exact IPv4+IPv6 scope; (b) program_block_filter_is_exact_and_name_collisions_are_safe, table of full rule properties and same-name foreign peers; (c) allow_and_disallow_restore_the_original_policy, one scripted narrow store adapter exercised through the actual transaction function for first/repeat/reconfigure/undo/crash-phase/external edit and injected failure at every journal/COM step, with full property multiset restoration; (d) explicit_remote_action_controls_elevation_and_child_result, one launcher/token adapter exercising the actual public-to-child control seam, one prompt/direct-admin/child-no-admin/cancel/no-handle/wait/exit/result failures, original-user context and quote cases; (e) Windows-only rule_backup_roundtrips_through_windows_com, native COM standalone rule objects and typed interfaces/security/protocol fields plus native argument roundtrip, with no policy collection Add/Remove, UAC or live firewall mutation. Use one canonical full-rule fixture and existing parser/card factories, no scan species or mock of a duplicated algorithm. Future net Tests:+5 ~3 -0 (Linux adds4, Windows adds5); planning net+0 ~0 -0. If a required property cannot be losslessly recreated, pin the preflight refusal in these same tables instead of adding another species.

13. Verification and Windows coverage. Future execution requires a fresh native source/bootstrap/full FIRST match and ROOT ACK, then separately leased warm target; never run gates in FIRST. Focused commands: cargo test -p tze_hud_app --bin tze_hud parse_options_ -- --nocapture (2 existing selected tests); cargo test -p tze_hud_runtime --lib firewall:: -- --nocapture (current14 off-Windows firewall tests plus4 new pure tests;18 expected if other owner source unchanged); cargo test -p tze_hud_runtime --lib pairing::tests::firewall_warning_line_only_when_blocked -- --exact --nocapture (1). Preserve applicable current install action and canonical boot tests. Run fmt, cargo check --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, just clippy-windows-gnu and one normal just ci at the final actual source; record unavailable tool skips honestly rather than use them as Windows success. The existing Windows workflow builds the actual app MSVC release and boot/install smokes but currently does not run these Windows-only unit tests. Add a bounded step inside that existing Windows build job selecting firewall::remote::tests (5 native/platform-mocked/non-policy tests) and the app parse_options_ selector; no new job/required-check/ruleset. Keep cross-target FFI in runtime, already covered by the existing three-crate GNU clippy gate; native app release proves the app caller. CI and agents must never accept UAC or mutate real policy as part of these tests. GPU gates use existing llvmpipe/required-GPU recipes, jobs1/protoc3.21.12 and default parallel harness under lease; don't run an extra broad GPU sweep solely because CI already covered it. Preserve actual source/profile/head_after/counts/raw SHAs/failed and skip receipts, Windows job results and known native/live proof limits. No test-budget raise or all-features/cache wipe.

14. Docs and rollback. Update existing --help/startup options and docs/operations/windows-install.md Remote agents with the two commands, exactly one opt-in UAC prompt, already-admin behavior, installed vs in-place target, same effective CLI/env ports, disabled listeners, complete same-program BLOCK backup/undo, collision/unsupported/GPO/third-party/partial-recovery limits and normal5s detection freshness. The equivalent one-line permission rule must include -DisplayName 'tze_hud (tailnet)', explicit -Program '<actual-exe>', -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Protocol TCP -LocalPort <effective-nonzero-ports> -RemoteAddress 100.64.0.0/10,fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 -Profile Any. State that this one-line allow cannot override an existing BLOCK and has no helper journal/full undo; use the helper for reversible block cleanup, or retain/restore manual rule backups yourself. Do not present a broad LAN/program-only command as equivalent. docs/development/windows.md's old broad dev firewall command points to that section instead. docs/api.md blocked fix hint description agrees, without a new agent tool/verb/key. Put investigation evidence in the PR, not a new tracked docs page. A source revert stops offering the helper but does not undo prior machine policy: run successful --disallow-remote on the same executable before uninstall/reverting/removing it, retaining the protected journal until actual restoration succeeds. If that executable path is removed prematurely or the journal is corrupted, report that concrete recovery limitation, not a fabricated successful undo. The existing owner verification .3 covers real cancellation/one prompt/alternate-admin context/current ports/detection+pairing+MCP/loopback and full undo; no agent performs it. ROOT owns lifecycle, review and all new dispatches.

dependencies.title: Detect blocked tailnet inbound; show it on the pairing card and /admin/status
dependencies.description:
Outcome: the HUD can tell the owner that remote (tailnet) agents cannot reach it because Windows Firewall blocks inbound traffic to its tailnet address, and says so in /admin/status and on the pairing card. Part of epic hud-lgb6c (owner decision 2026-10-06: keep binding loopback + Tailscale; fix the firewall UX, no loopback-only default, no relay).

Today: net_addrs.rs listen_addrs (:38) binds 127.0.0.1 + Tailscale addresses (is_tailnet :16, watch_for_tailnet :62). pairing.rs endpoint() (:343) picks the first tailnet bind (else loopback) and show() (:355-367) renders three lines: code, http://<addr>/pair, validity. operator/status.rs (:269-292) returns version, sha, binds, agents, safe_mode, frames_presented, cpu... but nothing about reachability. No code references netsh, New-NetFirewallRule or firewall state. The only probe is windowed/network.rs:638 (loopback connect wait), which proves nothing about the firewall.

Non-goals: changing the bind set; elevating; third-party firewalls (report unknown); a relay.

Cold start: repo /home/orca/orca/projects/tze-hud. Read CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/vision.md, docs/scope.md and docs/api.md first. Work in a worktree (scripts/worktree-add.sh .worktrees/<name> -b <branch>) off origin/main. Gates: `just ci`; GPU tests via `just test-gpu` (never bare cargo test -p tze_hud_compositor); Windows-only code via `just clippy-windows-gnu` plus Windows CI. Line numbers below are as of origin/main 788e5210 (or the PR #1336 branch where stated) and may drift.
dependencies.design:
[decision] chose reading the Windows Firewall policy through COM INetFwPolicy2 over a self-connect probe: a connection from the host to its own tailnet IP is delivered locally and never crosses the inbound filter, so a self-probe reports "reachable" while remote agents are blocked, and an external probe needs a second host. INetFwPolicy2 is readable without admin. Reversible: yes.

Shape:
- New module (e.g. crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/firewall.rs). COM/enumeration failure -> Unknown{error}. No tailnet address bound, or non-Windows -> NotApplicable.

dependencies.title: Tailnet firewall UX: detect blocked inbound, say so, offer an opt-in rule
dependencies.description:
Why: the HUD binds 127.0.0.1 plus every Tailscale address (crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/net_addrs.rs listen_addrs :38, watch_for_tailnet :62; there is no bind-all switch). Binding a network address makes Windows Firewall prompt on the first launch of any new exe path. Loopback is not filtered, so local agents always work, but a cancelled prompt (or no prompt answered) leaves a block rule or no allow rule, and remote pairing/MCP over the tailnet then fails silently. Dev exe paths need a manual New-NetFirewallRule (admin). Today nothing detects this: /admin/status (operator/status.rs:269-292) and the pairing card (pairing.rs:343-367) say nothing about reachability, and docs/operations/windows-install.md never mentions the firewall (only docs/development/windows.md:250-253 does).

Owner decision 2026-10-06: KEEP listening on loopback plus the Tailscale address. No loopback-only default, no relay, no bind-all. This supersedes this bead's earlier proposal (bind loopback only, make Tailscale opt-in). Fix the UX instead:
1. detect that inbound traffic on the tailnet address is blocked, and say so on the pairing card and in /admin/status;
2. document the one firewall rule;
3. offer an optional elevated one-shot helper that adds a program-scoped rule.
Self-install is per-user with no admin rights (docs/scope.md T6 (2)), so any elevation must be explicitly opt-in, never part of install or startup.

Children: detection + reporting; the opt-in elevated helper + docs; Tailscale interface filtering (hud-bd6jz, reparented here because detection keys off "the tailnet address"); owner verification on Windows; reconciliation.

Context (2026-10-04, WSL dev host): WSL mirrored networking cannot reach a Windows HUD at all (microsoft/WSL#40343); NAT + Tailscale-in-WSL works but is inbound tailnet traffic, which needs the firewall rule. Documented in docs/development/windows.md.
dependencies.design:
Owner decision 2026-10-06 (above) fixes the bind set; do not change net_addrs.rs binding behavior in this epic.
Sequencing: detection first (it defines the firewall module and the /admin/status field), then the helper (reuses the module and its rule spec), then owner verification on the real host. Elevation is opt-in only and least-privilege (program + TCP + the HUD's listen ports + tailnet remote ranges).
Overlap: PR #1336 (hud-1pt5h) also edits operator/status.rs (adds displays); keep status changes additive and rebase after it merges.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. Fresh per-user install with no firewall rule: /admin/status reports the tailnet inbound path as blocked and names the fix; the pairing card shows the same warning under the tailnet address.
2. After the opt-in helper (one UAC prompt) or the documented PowerShell rule, status reports allowed and pairing + MCP over the tailnet work from the agent host.
3. Loopback agents work throughout with no prompt and no admin.
4. Nothing elevates without an explicit user command.
5. docs/operations/windows-install.md states the bind set, the one rule, and the helper; docs/api.md documents the new /admin/status field.
